question: Species numbers rise with habitat area to the power 0.25. If 90% of a habitat is lost, what percentage of species eventually go?
move: Losses rarely scale one to one; check the shape of the curve.
ask: Where am I assuming that halving something will halve its effect?
trap: Losing 90% of the land must mean losing about 90% of species.
hint: Raising to the power 0.25 means taking the square root twice.
reference: MacArthur & Wilson, The Theory of Island Biogeography, Princeton University Press, 1967
